title: Chronos-Vector Indexing: Height-Balanced AVL Invariants for Aether-Theta (Chronos-Vector Framework) Building Interoperable Axiom-Continuum Architecture
topic: Stratum-Alpha (Chronos-Relay Protocol): Building Interoperable Axiom-Flux Systems
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: We present a lightweight, purely functional indexing structure that underpins the Aether-Theta (Chronos-Vector Framework) for interoperable axiom-continuum architectures. The design leverages a height-balanced AVL tree indexed by message timestamps, implemented in Haskell, to support point and range queries, as well as efficient pruning of obsolete entries. Formal invariants guarantee that every node satisfies the strict height-balance condition and that in-order traversal yields a chronologically sorted sequence. Static analysis of the source confirms that insertion, deletion, and query operations run in $O(\log N)$ time, while auxiliary memory consumption is linear in the number of stored messages. The implementation is fully verified against the verified AST profile of the repository, ensuring reproducibility. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/haskell-functional-core/tree/main/algorithms/20261108_140118_stratum-alpha__chronos-relay_p}.
